concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: visual direction board for ZipperCrew, an ordinary serious web application with a Babylon.js 3D crew room.
Create a landscape board, approximately 1536x1024. The upper 75% is one LARGE, composed in-app room screenshot; the bottom 25% is a quiet white strip showing the three full-body original character designs and brief role labels. Room viewport shows EXACTLY THREE characters, the same cast as the strip, each fully readable, about 18-23% of viewport height. Actual three-dimensional modeled geometry, stylized real-time game rendering achievable in a browser, smooth intentional sculpted forms, low/medium asset complexity, flat color blocks, one warm directional light, visible cast and received shadows, gentle ambient fill. No painterly rendering, no cinematic depth of field, no photoreal materials. Camera elevated three-quarter perspective around 30 degrees down, close enough to see faces; no strict isometric, distant dollhouse or floating cutaway diorama. Floor continues beyond near edge of view.
Simple game-level workspace: two small usable workstations positioned so characters remain visible, a shared brief surface, small coffee alcove, one window and one open doorway. Spacious clear walk routes and very little decoration. Characters dominate furniture. Small people in a larger physical world, but useful furniture fits them. World may have one oversized architectural detail to suggest scale, no giant prop clutter.
A single white LOCAL ACTIVITY bubble near Implementer reads exactly "Running tests…" then "14 passed · 2 failed". A physically thick cream message card with a folded corner labeled "Proposal" floats between Implementer and Reviewer, casting a subtle shadow, with a small gold seal; it is visually distinct from the bubble. No speech bubbles on other people. No trail of documents, no visible internal thought text.
A narrow restrained app bar at top says "ZipperCrew" at left and "Hub · 3 participants" at right. Small title and character role names at bottom. No fictional performance claims or engine logos.
Entirely original characters and room. Do not reproduce any copyrighted game, celebrity likeness, existing avatars, rabbit, paper person, generic robot, sandbox block geometry, office realism, showroom furniture, infant proportions or overly cute preschool aesthetics. Faces have simple broad brows, readable eyes and small mouths, matte color, no skin detail, fur or strand hair. Every character has expressive hands and can walk, sit, look, work and hold a small cup.
Direction title "01 · Little Ensemble". Storybook warmth realized as true simple 3D, mature whimsical creative energy. Three roles with radically different silhouettes:
HUMAN: original tiny creative adult with warm medium-brown complexion, lively asymmetric dark hair built from three big swept sculpted tufts, large expressive face, simple vermilion jacket with one yellow panel over cream shirt, indigo tapered trousers, oversized soft shoes. Broad curious gesture with one hand and notebook in other, no resemblance to a real person.
IMPLEMENTER: apricot-yellow upright amphibian-like maker with two broad swept-back head fins, blunt muzzle, two expressive big eyes, stout short legs, longer flexible arms and a short tapered tail; dark aubergine simple sleeveless work tunic, no tool clutter. Eager forward lean, one hand just lifted from keyboard, spring-loaded posture.
REVIEWER: calm deep-teal rounded mantle creature, broad low bell silhouette, a pale oval face inset in its broad upper body, big thoughtful horizontal eyebrows, short sturdy feet and distinct flexible arms. No shell, robot parts, paper or elaborate costume. Rust collar gives one restrained accent. Deliberate sideways head tilt over an open document.
Room is a small warm cream and muted sage workshop, softly rounded modular architecture, honey floor with no grain texture, ochre doorway arch, restrained blue work surfaces. A broad window sill hints at being tiny in a larger world. Human nearer shared brief at left, Implementer at shallow workstation center/back turned three-quarter so face reads, Reviewer at right with document and chair nearby. Warmth primarily comes from the cast, not architecture.
Bottom strip labels: "Human · curious gestures", "Implementer · quick hands", "Reviewer · measured pauses".

Use case: stylized-concept. Edit target: supplied ZipperCrew concept board. Keep the three character identities, roles, colors, expressive faces and bottom character strip. CORRECT THE LARGE ROOM VIEW.
The previous output is too close to the characters and too much like a rendered office. Change its camera to a higher elevated 35-degree-down composed perspective gameplay camera, pulled back to NORMAL GAMEPLAY SCALE: each standing character should occupy only 22-26% of the height of the UPPER ROOM VIEW, approximately 160 pixels tall in the roughly 650 pixel room area. The bottom strip is explicitly the close-up study; the upper view must demonstrate SMALL characters. Upper view has exactly three characters. Keep their faces readable by simple broad features. Remove all grain, fabric weave, carpet, glossy reflections, depth of field, photoreal shading, decorative plants, bookshelves, wall posters, slogans, trim, skyline. Small message card "Proposal" about one head tall between maker and reviewer; one modest white activity bubble with "Running tests…" and "14 passed · 2 failed". No giant floating document. concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ZipperCrew linked-room scalability study. Supplied reference board is ONLY a reference for the Little Ensemble character identities, simple flat materials and warm color palette; redesign the entire sheet layout.
Create a landscape 1536x1024 concept board with THREE EQUAL-WIDTH COLUMNS. Clean ivory background and restrained dark sans-serif typography. Title at top "Little Ensemble · More rooms, same crew scale".
The column headings are exactly "3 participants", "5 participants", "8 participants".
Each column has at top a small flat navigation diagram made of named rectangular room chips with connecting lines, then an EQUAL-SIZED LANDSCAPE GAME VIEWPORT, then a very short caption. These are THREE SEPARATE APP STATES, not rooms simultaneously viewed in one zoomed-out world. No bottom close-up character lineup.
Column 1 diagram: single chip "Hub · 3". Game viewport is "Hub": Human coral jacket + apricot maker + broad deep-teal reviewer from reference, exactly 3 small characters. Sparse warm room, two simple small work surfaces, brief surface, window, coffee shelf, an arch. Human glances at notebook, maker at keyboard, reviewer reads. One modest white activity bubble "Running tests…".
Column 2 diagram: chip "Hub · 3" connected to chip "Work · 2". Work chip highlighted with navy border, because it is the room being viewed. Game viewport is "Work": exactly 2 additional distinct crew members from same original stylistic family: taller blue bean-shaped creature and small russet crested maker. Simple two worktables, window, doorway. A thick cream card marked "Proposal" goes toward doorway, separate from any bubble. Caption "5 total · viewing Work".
Column 3 diagram: central chip "Hub · 2" connected separately to "Maker · 3" and "Quiet · 3". Quiet chip highlighted with navy border. Game viewport is "Quiet": exactly 3 characters, original deep-teal broad reviewer plus a slender dusty-mauve creature and a small slate-blue character; two reading surfaces, simple stools, window, arch. A cream Proposal packet resting visibly in a tiny arrival tray next to reviewer, restrained label "Awaiting receive". One small doorway badge "Maker · 1 new". Caption "8 total · viewing Quiet".
CRITICAL SCALE: ALL THREE VIEWPORTS ARE EXACTLY THE SAME DIMENSIONS, approximately 480 pixels wide by 340 pixels tall. EACH CHARACTER IS ONLY APPROXIMATELY 85-100 PIXELS TALL INSIDE ITS VIEWPORT. Same elevated three-quarter perspective game camera with about 30 degrees downward inclination, same implied focal distance, same world scale, same character screen height for all crew sizes. Small characters in a game level, not giant character portraits. Faces remain recognizable through big brows, eyes, silhouettes. Show floor space and shadows. Do not zoom out as crew size grows. Do not place all 5 or 8 in the single viewport. No miniature inset room views, no dollhouse diagram. Flat solid quiet environment colors, single warm directional light with clear shadows, no real wood, fabric, texture, detailed office furniture, plants, décor, slogans or photorealism.
Below three viewports, a clean narrow ordinary web UI example labeled "Room navigation" with buttons "Hub", "Maker", "Quiet" and text "Select a room · Select a participant · Follow a message". Small secondary text "Camera changes only when requested". At bottom one short line "Room population changes. Character size stays stable."
Original tiny whimsical but mature stylized 3D game characters, real geometric volume and floor shadows, subdued surroundings. Only original reference cast, no external franchise designs. Precise diagram counts: 3 = 3; 5 = 3 + 2; 8 = 2 + 3 + 3. No other text.
